01_tu_red_muted.label: TU red muted categorical
01_tu_red_muted.comment: Main recommendation for four estimator classes: TU red, muted rose, desaturated brown-gray, and blue-gray.

02_tu_red_scientific.label: TU red scientific contrast
02_tu_red_scientific.comment: Still red-led, but with cool and ochre accents for stronger distinction in line and scatter plots.

03_tu_red_pastel.label: TU red pastel
03_tu_red_pastel.comment: Softest palette. Good for filled bars and boxes, slightly weaker for thin lines.

04_tu_red_earth.label: TU red earth tones
04_tu_red_earth.comment: Warm, calm print palette with red, clay, olive-gray, and slate.

05_tu_red_monochrome.label: TU red monochrome sequence
05_tu_red_monochrome.comment: Useful when the four categories are ordered. Not ideal when categories must be equally distinct.

06_tu_red_print_safe.label: TU red print-safe
06_tu_red_print_safe.comment: More conservative and robust in grayscale or print. Less pastel, but still not poppy.

07_tu_red_muted_reordered.label: TU red muted reordered
07_tu_red_muted_reordered.comment: Same family as the current red-muted palette, but M2 is moved to blue-gray. This is the quickest fix when M1 and M2 must be separated clearly.

08_tu_red_cool_muted.label: TU red with cool muted accents
08_tu_red_cool_muted.comment: Red-led but with blue, olive, and brown-gray accents. Good for nominal model classes because the four hues are not just red shades.

09_tu_red_neutral_highcontrast.label: TU red and neutral contrast
09_tu_red_neutral_highcontrast.comment: Very restrained palette for print-heavy figures. Red marks the main model, while the other classes use graphite, blue-gray, and light gray.

10_user_bright_direct.label: Requested bright palette
10_user_bright_direct.comment: Uses the requested saturated red, purple, blue, and green exactly. Strong separation, but noticeably more colorful than the dissertation style.

11_user_bright_tempered.label: Requested palette, dissertation-tempered
11_user_bright_tempered.comment: A calmer version inspired by the requested colors. It keeps the red-purple-blue-green structure but lowers saturation for a less poppy scientific look.

12_tu_red_colorblind_safe.label: TU red plus colorblind-safe accents
12_tu_red_colorblind_safe.comment: Scientific/high-contrast option: TU red combined with blue, green, and ochre accents. Best candidate when lines overlap heavily.

13_tu_red_muted_purple_green.label: TU red muted with purple and soft green
13_tu_red_muted_purple_green.comment: Close to the current red-muted style, but the rose and brown-gray slots are replaced by muted purple and a softer light green for clearer M1/M2/M3 separation.

14_tu_red_muted_purple_m2.label: TU red muted with purple M2
14_tu_red_muted_purple_m2.comment: Minimal variant of the current red-muted palette: M1, M3, and M4 stay unchanged, while the rose M2 is replaced by muted purple.

15_default_cycler_red_green_orange_cyan.label: Default cycler red, green, orange, cyan
15_default_cycler_red_green_orange_cyan.comment: Direct test of the proposed Matplotlib cycler colors. Strongly separated and readable, but more saturated than the muted dissertation palettes.

16_eaai_extracted_light.label: EAAI extracted light fill palette
16_eaai_extracted_light.comment: Palette extracted from the EAAI figures: green, red, and blue as the main colours plus matching purple for a fourth class. Use the main colours for lines and outlines; use the fill colours for bars, boxes, and histograms.
